mainTopic: Chains of עדים זוממין, when עדים זוממין are punished, אין עונשין מן הדין, and how a group of witnesses counts as one testimony
overview: The amud opens by asking about רבי יהודה's view that a chain of עדים זוממין is a 'conspiracy'. רבי אבהו's answer is rejected. רבא's reading is challenged from the word 'בלבד', and that challenge stays a קשיא. Next comes a story of a woman whose first two sets of witnesses were caught lying. ריש לקיש says she is now suspect, while רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן say new witnesses are not suspect. The גמרא then shows that neither view depends on the רבי יהודה and רבנן argument. A new משנה teaches that עדים זוממין are executed only if they are caught after the verdict, against the צדוקים, who required that the accused already be dead. The גמרא brings בריבי's ruling that if the accused was already killed, the witnesses are not killed, because אין עונשין מן הדין. A ברייתא proves this from the full-sister verses, and also teaches that a prohibition cannot come from a קל וחומר either. Then comes the story of רבי יהודה בן טבאי, who wrongly executed a single עד זומם and regretted it all his life. Finally, a משנה learns from 'two or three witnesses' that a group of any size counts as one testimony, with views of the תנא קמא, רבי שמעון and רבי עקיבא, and a lesson about reward for joining a מצוה.

steps.title: If it's a conspiracy, why kill even the first set?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: if the chain of witnesses looks like a conspiracy, even the first set should not be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this is a conspiracy, then even the first set should not be killed either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יהודה's statement from the משנה. If he calls the whole thing a suspicious 'conspiracy,' why should the first set of witnesses be killed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the case is an איסטטית (a conspiracy), so we should not trust the later sets of witnesses. But the first set was made זוממין by the second set. If the second set is suspect, then the first set's punishment is also based on suspect testimony. So his logic seems to cancel out the punishment of the first set too.

keyTerms.meaning: A conspiracy or plotted group (from Greek); a suspicious setup
The first set of witnesses
Also not

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'אִי אִיסְטָטִית הִיא זוֹ' are quoting רבי יהודה from the משנה. They are not the גמרא's own claim.

phrases.english: If this is a conspiracy,
phrases.notes: These are רבי יהודה's words in the משנה about a chain of witness sets, each one proving the set before it was lying.

phrases.english: then even the first set should also not [be killed]!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִיסְטָטִית הִיא זוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ כַּת רִאשׁוֹנָה נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens analysis of רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that only the first set is killed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the case a conspiracy makes all the testimony suspect. That includes the testimony that made the first set זוממין.

steps.title: The first set was already killed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that רבי יהודה means the first set had already been killed before the later sets came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is a case where they already killed them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question. The first set is mentioned only because it was already killed before the conspiracy became clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is not saying the first set should be killed. He is describing what had already happened. By the time more sets showed up and made the case look suspicious, the first set had been killed. From then on, nobody else is killed.

keyTerms.meaning: They acted first and already killed them

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said:
It is where they already went ahead and killed [them].
phrases.notes: He means the court had already killed the first set before the later sets of witnesses came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: שֶׁקָדְמוּ וְהָרְגוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה rules that the first set should be killed despite the conspiracy
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה is describing a first set that was already killed. He is not ruling that they should be killed.

steps.title: What already happened is not a law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי אבהו's answer, since describing a past event teaches nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What happened, happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבהו. It is pointless for רבי יהודה to tell us about a killing that already took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה teaches what should be done. If the first set was already killed, nothing can be done about it, so there is no reason to state it as part of a ruling. This makes רבי אבהו's reading hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was; a past event cannot be undone, so stating it adds no law

phrases.english: What happened, happened!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דַהֲוָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's explanation that the first set was already killed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A past event is not a law. There would be no reason to say it in the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: one set is killed, many sets are not
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רבי יהודה differently. One set made זוממין is killed, but if there is more than one set, none are killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what he means: If there is only one set, it is killed. If there are more, they are not killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רבי אבהו's approach and gives a new reading of רבי יהודה. The conspiracy idea only applies when many sets are involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a normal case, one set is made זוממין and is killed. But once a chain of several sets appears, it looks like a conspiracy, and no set at all is killed, not even the first. This fully answers the first question in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
One set of witnesses
More
They are not killed

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said, this is what he means:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא כַּת אַחַת – נֶהֱרֶגֶת,
phrases.english: if it is only one set, it is killed;
if there are more, they are not killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי אבהו's rejected answer with a new reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה kills the first set even in a chain
steps.terutzMaskana: In a chain of several sets, no one is killed. Only a lone set is killed.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה said 'only'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from the word 'בלבד' in רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'only'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה said 'only the first set alone is killed.' That wording does not fit רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בלבד' (only) means there were other sets who were not killed while the first set was. That describes a case with several sets where the first set is killed. But רבא said that when there are several sets, nobody is killed.

keyTerms.meaning: Only, alone

phrases.english: But he said 'only'!
phrases.notes: The word comes from רבי יהודה in the משנה: 'only the first set alone is killed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא ״בִּלְבַד״ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that no one is killed when there are several sets
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Only the first set' assumes several sets exist and that the first is killed. That contradicts רבא.

steps.title: The question stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the challenge against רבא remains unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'קשיא' and stops. The challenge from the word 'only' has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the question is real and unresolved, but the view is not fully thrown out. This is weaker than a תיובתא, which completely refutes a view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's 'conspiracy' view was explained two ways. רבי אבהו said the first set was already killed, and that was rejected. רבא said one set is killed but many sets are not, and that is left with an unanswered question from the word 'only.'
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end of a discussion is not the same as 'תיובתא'. קשיא leaves a question open. תיובתא knocks the view down.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion, leaving step 5's challenge unanswered
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's reading stays as it is, with an unresolved question from the word 'בלבד'.

steps.title: A woman whose witnesses were caught lying twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells of a woman whose first two sets of witnesses were proven liars. Her third set was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman who brought witnesses, and they were proven liars. She brought witnesses, and they were proven liars. She went and brought other witnesses who were not proven liars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the idea of suspicious repeated testimony. This sets up a debate about whether to trust the third set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the משנה's chain of witnesses, here one person keeps bringing witnesses who turn out false. The question is whether her history makes the third, unchallenged set suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
Witnesses
They were proven liars
Others

phrases.english: There was a certain woman who brought witnesses, and they were proven liars;
she brought witnesses, and they were proven liars.
She went and brought other witnesses
who were not proven liars.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּאֲתַאי סָהֲדִי וְאִישְׁתַּקּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story linked to the theme of suspicious repeated testimony
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case: two false sets of witnesses, then a third set that was not disproven.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: she is now suspect
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that the woman has an established status of dishonesty, so her third set is not trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This woman has become established as suspect.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his ruling. Because she brought false witnesses twice, we no longer trust her witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that happens repeatedly creates a חזקה, a presumption. Twice using false witnesses gives her a presumption of bringing liars, so the third set is rejected even though no one disproved them.

keyTerms.meaning: She has become established (in a presumption)
A presumption based on a repeated pattern

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
This woman has become established [as suspect].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הוּחְזְקָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third set is rejected because the woman has a presumption of dishonesty.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the whole Jewish people are not suspect
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר objects that her bad record does not make these new witnesses liars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: If she is established as suspect, are all of Israel established as suspect?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges ריש לקיש. Even if she is suspect, the new witnesses are separate people with no record of lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony comes from the witnesses, not from her. Her pattern does not prove anything about these particular witnesses, who are ordinary trustworthy Jews. So the third set should be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: All of the Jewish people
Is it so? (a question word, used for 'are they?')

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said to him:
If she is established [as suspect],
are all of Israel established [as suspect]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אִם הִיא הוּחְזְקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rejection of the third set
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her presumption applies only to her, not to the new and unrelated witnesses.

steps.title: The same case comes before רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Later, a similar case came up while they sat before רבי יוחנן, and ריש לקיש gave the same ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were sitting before רבי יוחנן, and a case like this came before them. ריש לקיש said: This woman has become established as suspect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene for a second round of the same debate, this time in front of their teacher רבי יוחנן. ריש לקיש repeats his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeat matters because the response will now come from רבי יוחנן himself. ריש לקיש has not changed his mind after hearing רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Once, on another occasion
Sitting before him (as students)
An incident or case

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין הָווּ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Once they were sitting before רבי יוחנן,
phrases.notes: 'They' are ריש לקיש and רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: and a case like this came before them.
ריש לקיש said:
This woman has become established [as suspect].

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין הָווּ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the debate in a new setting, before רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש again rules that the woman is suspect.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gives רבי אלעזר's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש with the same words רבי אלעזר had used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: If she is established as suspect, are all of Israel established as suspect?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's view, word for word the way רבי אלעזר did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבי אלעזר's objection was really רבי יוחנן's teaching. The view that the new witnesses are trusted now has רבי יוחנן's authority behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: They have become established (plural)
This (woman)

steps.whyThisMatters: For רבי יוחנן, the trustworthiness of new witnesses is judged on their own, not by the record of the person who brings them.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said to him:
If this woman is established [as suspect],
are all of Israel established [as suspect]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִם הוּחְזְקָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's repeated ruling, the same way as step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the third set is rejected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman's suspicion does not carry over to the new witnesses.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is upset with רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש glares at רבי אלעזר for not saying that his objection came from רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He turned and looked angrily at רבי אלעזר and said to him: You heard these words from בר נפחא, and you did not tell them to me in his name?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש realizes that רבי אלעזר's objection was really רבי יוחנן's teaching. He complains that רבי אלעזר did not say so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had ריש לקיש known the source was רבי יוחנן, he would have taken it more seriously. The story shows the importance of quoting a teaching in the name of the one who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned
He looked at him
Angrily, with a bad look
Son of the smith; a nickname for רבי יוחנן
In his name

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש holds that a woman who twice brought false witnesses is suspect, so her third set is rejected. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן hold that her record does not make new witnesses suspect.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בר נפחא' is not a different sage. It is a nickname for רבי יוחנן himself.

phrases.english: He turned and looked angrily at רבי אלעזר,
phrases.notes: 'He' is ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: and said to him:
You heard these words from בר נפחא,
and you did not tell them to me in his name?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר חַזְיֵהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בִּישׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי יוחנן's answer by linking it to רבי אלעזר's earlier answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר's objection was רבי יוחנן's teaching, and a teaching should be quoted in the name of the one who said it. According to רבי יוחנן, a woman's past false witnesses do not make new witnesses suspect.

steps.title: Is this the same as the רבי יהודה and רבנן argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests linking ריש לקיש to רבי יהודה and רבי יוחנן to רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that ריש לקיש ruled like רבי יהודה, and רבי יוחנן ruled like רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to connect the argument we just saw to an older argument in the משנה. This sets up the next two steps, which will push back on that link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, one pair of witnesses showed that several sets of witnesses were זוממין. רבי יהודה became suspicious of that pair, while רבנן trusted them. The גמרא suggests that ריש לקיש's suspicion of the woman matches רבי יהודה, and רבי יוחנן's trust matches רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא often rejects)
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.confusionAlert: A לֵימָא question usually gets rejected. Don't treat this link as the conclusion.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Shall we say that Reish Lakish ruled like Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Yochanan ruled like the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא steps back and tries to place the dispute inside an older argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן dispute simply repeat the רבי יהודה and רבנן dispute?

steps.title: ריש לקיש can even agree with רבנן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's view fits רבנן too, because here the woman is actively hunting for witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש could tell you: What I said holds even according to רבנן. רבנן only trusted the witnesses there because nobody was going around looking for witnesses. But here, this woman is the one going around looking for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש does not have to hold like רבי יהודה. He can agree with רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, no interested party was going around collecting witnesses, so there was no special reason for suspicion. Here the woman herself keeps bringing set after set of witnesses. That gives real reason to suspect she is hiring them, so even רבנן would not trust her third set.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said it in this case (it limits a ruling)
Goes around searching or hunting
There (the other case) / here (our case)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish could say to you:
What I said to you holds even according to the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: The Rabbis only said their view there,
where there is no one going around searching.
phrases.notes: He means no one was searching for witnesses to testify for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, אִיכָּא הָא דְּקָא מְהַדְּרָא.
phrases.english: But here, there is this woman who is going around searching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי לָךְ אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first half of the proposed link from step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that ריש לקיש needs רבי יהודה's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored a key difference: here an interested party is actively hunting for witnesses.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן can even agree with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's view fits רבי יהודה too, because the new witnesses may really know what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could tell you: What I said holds even according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה was only suspicious there because we ask, "Was the whole world standing next to these two witnesses?" But here, maybe these witnesses really know the testimony, and those earlier ones did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן does not have to hold like רבנן. He can agree with רבי יהודה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה was suspicious because one pair claimed to have been with every single set of witnesses, which is hard to believe. In our case, different witnesses are testifying each time. The earlier sets being caught lying says nothing about the new set, who may truly know the facts.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say the whole world...? (a question showing something is far-fetched)
Testimony
They know

steps.whatToRemember: Neither אמורא has to depend on the רבי יהודה and רבנן argument. Our woman's case has its own features: she is hunting for witnesses, but the witnesses are different people each time.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan could say to you:
What I said holds even according to Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said his view there,
because we say: "Is that to say the whole world
was standing next to these witnesses?"
But here, these witnesses may know the testimony,
and those witnesses did not know the testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second half of the proposed link from step 13, which completes the rejection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי יוחנן needs רבנן's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's suspicion came from one pair claiming to be everywhere, and that is missing in our case.

steps.title: New משנה: עדים זוממין are executed only after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: עדים זוממין are killed only if they are caught after the verdict, and not, as the צדוקים say, only after the accused was executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: עדים זוממין are not executed unless the verdict has been finished. The צדוקים say they are executed only once the accused has actually been killed, as the verse says, "A life for a life."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the timing for when עדים זוממין get the death penalty, and it mentions the צדוקים' opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the court has finished the verdict against the accused, catching the witnesses as זוממין makes them liable to death. The צדוקים read "נפש תחת נפש" literally: the witnesses die only if their victim already died. The משנה brings this view in order to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting witnesses, shown to be lying because they were elsewhere at the time
Until the verdict is finished
צדוקים, a sect that rejected the oral tradition
A life for a life

steps.confusionAlert: The צדוקים' view is not the הלכה. The משנה quotes them so it can argue against them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the time window for הזמה punishment. The window opens once the verdict is final, and it does not depend on whether the accused was executed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The plotting witnesses are not executed
unless the verdict has been finished.
For the Sadducees say: only once the accused is killed,
as it is said: "A life for a life."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:23

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין הָעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין נֶהֱרָגִין עַד שֶׁיִּגָּמֵר הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The previous discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין are executed only if they are caught after the verdict is finished. The צדוקים say only after the accused is killed, based on "נפש תחת נפש."

steps.title: The חכמים prove the accused can still be alive
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים prove from 'as he plotted to do to his brother' that עדים זוממין are punished while the accused is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to the צדוקים: Doesn't the verse say 'do to him as he plotted to do to his brother'? That means the brother is still alive!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer the צדוקים, who said the witnesses are killed only after the accused was executed. They bring a פסוק showing the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'plotted' (זמם) means the plan was not carried out. So the Torah is describing a case where the accused is still alive, and it still punishes the witnesses. That disproves the צדוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A sect that rejected the Oral Torah's way of reading the פסוקים
Plotted or planned (but did not carry out)
And look, his brother is still alive

phrases.english: The Sages said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the צדוקים from the last step.

phrases.english: But wasn't it already stated:
"And you shall do to him as he plotted
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

phrases.english: to do to his brother",
and here his brother is still alive!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם חֲכָמִים: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the חכמים's side against the צדוקים' view quoted in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: עדים זוממין are punished even if the accused was not executed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 19:19, 'as he plotted to do to his brother'.

steps.title: Then why does the Torah say 'a life for a life'?
steps.stepSummary: If the accused is alive, what does the phrase 'a life for a life' come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the Torah say 'a life for a life'?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים set up their own question. 'A life for a life' sounds like a life must have been lost, so what is it teaching?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase is probably what the צדוקים relied on. The חכמים have to show it has a different meaning that fits their view.

keyTerms.meaning: A life for a life
Why was it stated? (asking what a phrase comes to teach)

phrases.english: And if so, why is it stated:
"A life for a life"?
phrases.notes: שמות 21:23

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the other פסוק is for, now that step 17 showed the accused can be alive.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'a life for a life' teach, if not that the accused must be dead?

steps.title: 'A life for a life' means only after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: The phrase teaches that the witnesses are killed only if they are caught after the verdict was given, not as soon as their testimony was accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they are killed as soon as the court accepted their testimony. So the Torah says 'a life for a life': they are not killed until the verdict is final.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer their own question. 'A life for a life' sets the earliest point at which the witnesses can be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only once the court has sentenced the accused is his life really at stake. Before that, the witnesses are not killed. So both פסוקים fit together: no death is required, but a final verdict is.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Therefore the verse says
That the verdict is finished

steps.whatToRemember: עדים זוממין are killed only if they are caught after the verdict, even though the accused is still alive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact window for הזמה: after the verdict, before the execution.

phrases.english: One might have thought that from the time their testimony was accepted
they are killed?
Therefore the verse says: "A life for a life,"
so they are not killed
until the verdict is finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ עֵדוּתָן יֵהָרְגוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'A life for a life' teaches that the witnesses are killed only after the verdict, not as soon as their testimony was accepted.

steps.title: If they succeeded in killing him, the witnesses are not killed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בריבי: if the accused was not yet killed, the witnesses are executed; if he was already killed, they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בריבי says: If they did not kill him, they are killed. If they did kill him, they are not killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה with a ruling that sounds surprising: עדים זוממין whose plot worked escape the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the חכמים's reading of 'as he plotted': the punishment is written for a plot, not for a finished act. Once the accused is dead, the case falls outside what the Torah wrote.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The distinguished one', a title for a scholar
They are executed

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a typo. The witnesses whose lie worked really are NOT killed by the court, even though that sounds backwards.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught: The distinguished one says:
If they did not kill – they are killed,
if they killed – they are not killed.
phrases.notes: He means: if the accused was already executed because of their false testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, בְּרִיבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא and takes the משנה's idea one step further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין are executed only if the accused was not yet killed; if he was killed, they are not executed.

steps.title: His father objects: isn't it a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: בריבי's father argues that if a failed plot earns death, a successful one certainly should.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father said: My son, isn't this a קל וחומר?
steps.whatsHappening: The father challenges the ruling using simple logic from the lighter case to the more serious one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting someone wrongly killed is worse than only trying to. If the Torah punishes the lesser case with death, logic says the worse case should be punished too.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a more serious one
My son

phrases.english: His father said:
My son, isn't it a kal vachomer?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנִי, לָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: בריבי's ruling that witnesses who caused an execution are not executed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a failed plot is punished by death, a successful one should be punished all the more.

steps.title: We do not punish based on logic
steps.stepSummary: בריבי answers that his father himself taught that a punishment cannot come from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You taught us, our teacher, that we do not punish based on a logical argument.
steps.whatsHappening: בריבי defends his ruling. He agrees the logic is strong, but says it cannot be used to give a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A punishment must be written in the Torah itself. Since the Torah only wrote the death penalty for a plot that did not succeed, we cannot add the successful case by logic.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not punish based on a logical argument
Our teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: אין עונשין מן הדין is a general rule across the whole תורה: a punishment must be written in a פסוק and cannot be learned from a קל וחומר. The same ברייתא later adds that a prohibition cannot be learned that way either (step 29).

phrases.english: He said to him:
You have taught us, our teacher,
that we do not punish based on a logical argument.
phrases.notes: Here 'הדין' means a קל וחומר, not a court ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִימַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁאֵין עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits what the קל וחומר can do: it cannot create a punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר should make the witnesses who succeeded liable to death.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because אין עונשין מן הדין, only what the Torah wrote, the failed plot, is punished.

steps.title: The Torah wrote a separate verse for a full sister
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the Torah wrote a separate verse to punish relations with a full sister, even though a קל וחומר could have taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'A man who takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter' covers only a half sister. Where do we learn a full sister? The verse says: 'he uncovered his sister's nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: בריבי brings a ברייתא to prove his rule. First it shows that the punishment for a full sister comes from its own phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the פסוק covers only half sisters. The full sister needs the extra words 'he uncovered his sister's nakedness.' The next step explains why that proves the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from this verse)
From where do we learn it?
A forbidden relationship

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"A man who takes his sister,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother":
I only know of the daughter of his father
who is not the daughter of his mother,
and the daughter of his mother who is not the daughter of his father.
The daughter of both his mother and his father, from where?
The verse says: "He has uncovered his sister's nakedness."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִקַּח אֶת אֲחֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the rule in step 22.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 20:17 about a man and his sister.

steps.title: The Torah did not rely on logic, so neither can we
steps.stepSummary: A full sister could have been learned by קל וחומר, yet the Torah wrote it anyway. This proves that a punishment cannot come from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even without the verse I could have argued: if there is a punishment for a half sister, then certainly for a full sister! So you learn that we do not punish based on logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its point. It shows that an obvious קל וחומר existed, and the Torah still did not rely on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a קל וחומר could create a punishment, the extra words in the פסוק would not be needed. Since the Torah wrote them, punishments must be written explicitly. That backs up בריבי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I could prove it by logic
Isn't it all the more so?
So you have learned

steps.whatToRemember: אין עונשין מן הדין: the Torah wrote the full-sister punishment even though a קל וחומר was available. So עדים זוממין whose plot succeeded are not executed, because the Torah only wrote the punishment for a plot.

phrases.english: Even if it had not been stated,
I could have it from logic:

phrases.aramaic: אִם עָנַשׁ עַל בַּת אָבִיו שֶׁלֹּא בַּת אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: If He punished for the daughter of his father who is not the daughter of his mother,
and the daughter of his mother who is not the daughter of his father –

phrases.aramaic: בַּת אָבִיו וּבַת אִמּוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then the daughter of both his father and his mother, all the more so?
So you have learned
that we do not punish based on a logical argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵאָמֵר יֵשׁ לִי בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of step 23 and draws the rule from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A punishment cannot be derived from a קל וחומר. That is why בריבי's ruling stands against his father's objection.

steps.title: We have the punishment, but where is the warning?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says it has a source for the punishment of a full sister. Now it asks for the source of the warning (אזהרה).
steps.simpleTranslation: We have heard the punishment. Where do we get the warning from?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and asks a new question. This sets up the next move, where a פסוק will be brought for the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Torah law, a punishment needs two things: a punishment (עונש) and a separate warning that the act is forbidden (אזהרה). The ברייתא already has the punishment from ויקרא 20:17. Now it looks for the warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishment: the penalty the Torah gives for an act
Warning: the Torah's statement that the act is forbidden
From where? (asking for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts. A punishment verse alone is not enough. The Torah also needs a verse that forbids the act. Here the ברייתא is looking for that second verse.

phrases.english: We have heard the punishment,
phrases.notes: This is the punishment for a full sister, from the פסוק in step 23 (ויקרא 20:17).

phrases.english: from where do we get the warning?

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹנֶשׁ שָׁמַעְנוּ, אַזְהָרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. It moves from the punishment to the warning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the prohibition (אזהרה) against relations with a sister.

steps.title: The warning for a sister from ויקרא 18:9
steps.stepSummary: The warning comes from the פסוק 'the nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a פסוק that forbids relations with a sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'daughter of your father OR daughter of your mother'. Read simply, that means a half-sister on either side. This wording will lead to the next question about a full sister.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (brings a verse as the source)
Forbidden relations ('nakedness')

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:9

phrases.english: "The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father
or the daughter of your mother."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתְךָ בַת אָבִיךָ אוֹ בַת אִמֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 18:9 gives the warning against relations with a sister.

steps.title: That covers half-sisters, but what about a full sister?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as covering only half-sisters. It asks where the warning for a full sister comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only teaches a father's daughter who is not his mother's daughter, or a mother's daughter who is not his father's daughter. Where do we learn the warning for a sister who is both his father's daughter and his mother's daughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a gap in the פסוק and asks for another source. This sets up the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק says 'OR', the ברייתא reads it as a sister from only one parent. A full sister, from both parents, is not clearly included, so a new source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (this verse teaches only this narrow case)
A full sister: same father and same mother

phrases.english: I only have
the daughter of his father who is not the daughter of his mother,
and the daughter of his mother who is not the daughter of his father.
The daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּת אָבִיו שֶׁלֹּא בַּת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the פסוק of step 26 and asks about the case it leaves out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the warning against relations with a full sister.

steps.title: The warning for a full sister from ויקרא 18:11
steps.stepSummary: A separate פסוק, 'the daughter of your father's wife, born of your father, she is your sister', gives the warning for a full sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born of your father, she is your sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second פסוק that covers a full sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק speaks of a sister who is the daughter of your father AND of your father's wife. That is a full sister. So the Torah gave a separate warning just for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Born of your father

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:11

phrases.english: "The nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife,
born of your father,
she is your sister."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עֶרְוַת בַּת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיךָ מוֹלֶדֶת אָבִיךָ אֲחוֹתְךָ הִוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 18:11 gives the warning against relations with a full sister.

steps.title: A warning cannot come from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: A full sister could have been learned by a קל וחומר from half-sisters, yet the Torah wrote a separate פסוק. This shows that a warning cannot be learned from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even before the פסוק was said, I could have learned it by logic: if he is warned about his mother's daughter who is not his father's daughter, and his father's daughter who is not his mother's daughter, then surely he is warned about a sister who is both! So you have learned that we do not create a warning from logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the second פסוק was not needed if logic could teach it. From this it concludes that a warning cannot come from a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reasoning as step 24, now applied to the warning instead of the punishment. If a קל וחומר were enough, the Torah would not have needed ויקרא 18:11. Since the Torah wrote it anyway, a warning must come from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From logic, here meaning a קל וחומר
Isn't it all the more so? (how a קל וחומר is stated)
A warning (prohibition) cannot be created from a קל וחומר
Even before (without) the verse saying it

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of a Torah punishment need a פסוק. The punishment cannot come from a קל וחומר (step 24), and the warning cannot come from a קל וחומר either.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof for the full-sister case. It shows the rule against learning from a קל וחומר covers the prohibition itself, not only the penalty.

phrases.english: Even before it was said,
phrases.notes: He means: even without the פסוק for a full sister.

phrases.english: I have it from logic:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִם הוּזְהַר עַל בַּת אִמּוֹ
phrases.english: If he was warned about the daughter of his mother
who is not the daughter of his father,
and the daughter of his father who is not the daughter of his mother,
then the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother,
is it not all the more so?
So you have learned
that we do not create a warning from logic.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵאָמֵר יֵשׁ לִי מִן הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the extra פסוק of step 28 to prove the rule, the same way step 24 did for the punishment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אין מזהירין מן הדין: a prohibition cannot be learned from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: The rule covers מלקות too, through 'רשע'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא extends the rule to people who get מלקות. It uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'רשע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this for people who get lashes? The verse says 'wicked' and 'wicked'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how we know the rule also applies to lashes, not only to the death penalty. It answers with a word that appears in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'רשע' appears about someone who gets the death penalty and also about someone who gets lashes. This connection, a גזירה שוה, carries over the rule: just as death cannot come from a קל וחומר, lashes cannot either.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are liable to lashes
Wicked person, the shared word in the two פסוקים
Linking two laws through the same word that appears in both

phrases.english: Those liable to lashes, from where?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know that lashes also can't be learned from a קל וחומר?

phrases.english: The verse says "wicked" and "wicked."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:31 (death penalty) and דברים 25:2 (lashes).

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיבֵי מַלְקִיּוֹת מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule from the death penalty to מלקות.
steps.raayaObject: That lashes are not given based on a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from 'רשע' (במדבר 35:31 and דברים 25:2).

steps.title: The rule covers גלות too, through 'רוצח'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא extends the rule to people who go into exile. It uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'רוצח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this for people who go into exile? It comes from 'murderer' and 'murderer'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by applying the rule to גלות too, using a shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'רוצח' is used both for someone who kills on purpose and for someone who kills by accident and goes into exile. The link teaches that exile, like the death penalty, cannot come from a קל וחומר. So no type of punishment is learned from a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are liable to exile (an accidental killer)
Killer, the shared word in the two פסוקים
It is derived (through a גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: No punishment at all (death, lashes or exile) and no prohibition can be learned from a קל וחומר. This is why בריבי said the witnesses who already caused a death are not killed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the support for בריבי's position (step 22). Every kind of punishment needs an explicit source, not logic.

phrases.english: Those liable to exile, from where?
It is derived from "murderer" and "murderer."
phrases.notes: The word appears for one who kills on purpose (במדבר 35:21) and one who kills by accident (במדבר 35:11).

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיבֵי גָּלִיּוֹת מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Does for exile what step 30 did for lashes.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן טבאי executes an עד זומם to refute the צדוקים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי יהודה בן טבאי killed an עד זומם while the accused was still alive. He did it to prove the צדוקים wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי יהודה בן טבאי said, 'I swear I killed a conspiring witness.' He did it to uproot the view of the צדוקים, who said conspiring witnesses are killed only after the accused has already been killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא with a story. A judge describes how he executed a lying witness, an עד זומם, to prove the צדוקים wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים held that עדים זוממין are punished only if the accused was actually executed. The חכמים hold the reverse: they are punished when the accused has not yet been killed. To show this publicly, רבי יהודה בן טבאי executed an עד זומם while the accused was still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness proven false, because other witnesses say he was somewhere else at the time
Sadducees, a group that rejected the חכמים' tradition of the Oral Torah
The accused person who was on trial
An oath: 'May I not see the comfort of Israel if this is not true'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. The צדוקים said: punish the witnesses only after the accused was killed. The חכמים say: punish them only while the accused has not been killed.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Tabbai said:
May I [not] see the consolation
phrases.notes: This is a way of swearing: 'May I not see Israel's comfort if what I say isn't true.'

phrases.english: if I did not kill a conspiring witness.
to remove from the hearts of the Sadducees
who would say:
Conspiring witnesses are not killed
unless the accused has been killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of learning warnings and brings a story about the punishment of עדים זוממין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Against the צדוקים, an עד זומם can be executed even though the accused was not killed

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח says an innocent man was killed
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח tells him that he shed innocent blood. Witnesses are punished only when both of them are proven זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן שטח said to him: 'I swear you shed innocent blood! The חכמים said that conspiring witnesses are not killed, and not given lashes, unless both of them are proven conspirators.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון בן שטח challenges what רבי יהודה בן טבאי did. He says the execution was a terrible mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן טבאי was right about the timing of the punishment. But he missed another rule: הזמה works only when both witnesses are caught. He had caught only one, so that witness was not liable and his death was unjust. The rule applies both to death and to lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Innocent blood, the killing of someone who did not deserve to die
That both witnesses are proven זוממין
They receive lashes (מלקות)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of עדים זוממין: a single witness who is proven false is not punished, because the testimony of a pair stands or falls together.

phrases.english: Shimon ben Shatach said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרְאֶה בְּנֶחָמָה אִם לֹא שָׁפַכְתָּ דָּם נָקִי,
phrases.english: May I [not] see the consolation if you did not shed innocent blood!
For the Sages said:
Conspiring witnesses are not killed
unless both of them are proven conspirators,
and they are not flogged unless both of them are proven conspirators.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the execution described in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The execution of a single עד זומם by רבי יהודה בן טבאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הזמה requires both witnesses to be proven false. Only one was, so he was not liable.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן טבאי accepts the rebuke
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן טבאי immediately agrees never again to issue a ruling except in front of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, רבי יהודה בן טבאי took upon himself that he would issue rulings only in the presence of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן טבאי admits his mistake. He limits his own authority so that it cannot happen again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue back, which shows he accepted that the rebuke was correct. From now on, every ruling he gives will be checked by שמעון בן שטח.

keyTerms.meaning: He took upon himself a commitment
Issues a halachic ruling
Immediately

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד קִבֵּל עָלָיו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
phrases.english: Immediately Rabbi Yehuda ben Tabbai took upon himself
that he would not issue a ruling
except before Shimon ben Shatach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד קִבֵּל עָלָיו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יהודה בן טבאי accepted the challenge of the previous step
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה בן טבאי admitted the error and would rule only in front of שמעון בן שטח

steps.title: He weeps on the witness's grave all his life
steps.stepSummary: For the rest of his life, רבי יהודה בן טבאי lay on the grave of the executed witness. People heard a voice and thought it was the dead man's.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the days of רבי יהודה בן טבאי, he would lie on the grave of that witness, and his voice was heard. The people thought it was the voice of the man who had been killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with his regret. It also sets up a question: whose voice were people hearing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He kept lying on the grave and crying out, asking forgiveness. The people heard crying and assumed it came from the dead witness himself, as if he were complaining. This misunderstanding leads into the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Lies stretched out, prostrating himself
The one who was killed
They thought, they assumed

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל יָמָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
phrases.english: And all the days of Rabbi Yehuda ben Tabbai

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מִשְׁתַּטֵּחַ עַל קִבְרוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ הָעֵד,
phrases.english: he would prostrate himself on the grave of that witness,
and his voice was heard,
and the people thought to say:
It is the voice of the executed man.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל יָמָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story, showing how deep his regret was

steps.title: He proves the voice is his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן טבאי says the voice is his. The proof: after he dies, the voice will stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'It is my own voice. You will know it, because tomorrow he will die and his voice will not be heard anymore.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן טבאי corrects the people. He gives a test that will prove the voice is his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is simple: if the voice stops once he dies, it must have been his all along. He speaks about himself as 'he' as a way of avoiding saying 'I will die.'

keyTerms.meaning: You will know, here is the proof
Tomorrow, meaning some day in the future
It is my own voice

phrases.english: He said: It is my own voice.
Know this: tomorrow he will die,
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבי יהודה בן טבאי himself. He avoids saying 'I will die.'

phrases.english: and his voice will not be heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: קוֹלִי שֶׁלִּי הוּא, תֵּדְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the people's mistaken assumption from the previous step
steps.raayaObject: That the voice heard at the grave belongs to רבי יהודה בן טבאי, not to the dead witness
steps.raayaSupportSource: The voice will stop after he dies

steps.title: רב אחא shows the proof does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא points out two other reasons the voice could stop. So the silence does not prove the voice was his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: Maybe the dead witness faced him in judgment in Heaven. Or maybe רבי יהודה בן טבאי made peace with him. Either way the voice would stop.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא pushes back on the proof in the story. The voice stopping after the death could have another explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the voice belonged to the dead witness, it could stop once רבי יהודה בן טבאי died. It might stop because the witness finally confronted him before the heavenly court, so he no longer needed to cry out. Or it might stop because the two made peace there. Since the silence fits both readings, it proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
He stood with him in judgment, he confronted him at trial
Alternatively
He appeased him, he made peace with him

steps.whatToRemember: The story teaches that הזמה requires both witnesses to be proven false. It also shows how seriously a judge must take a mistaken death sentence. The 'proof' that the voice was his own is rejected, because the silence after his death has other possible explanations.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
Perhaps he stood with him in judgment,
phrases.notes: Meaning the dead witness took him to trial in Heaven, so there was no more reason to cry out.

phrases.english: or else he appeased him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: דִּלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in the previous step
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof that the voice was רבי יהודה בן טבאי's. The story's halacha is not touched.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The voice stopping after his death fits other explanations: a heavenly trial, or making peace.

steps.title: Why does the verse mention three witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes the פסוק about two or three witnesses and asks why 'three' is needed if two are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'By two witnesses or three witnesses the one who is to die shall be put to death.' If testimony is valid with two, why did the verse spell out three?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It quotes a פסוק and asks why the word 'three' is there, which sets up the answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are already enough to make an עדות valid. So mentioning 'three' looks extra. The משנה assumes an extra word must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Testimony
Stands, is valid
The verse spelled out (a specific detail)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"By the mouth of two witnesses
phrases.notes: דברים 17:6

phrases.english: or three witnesses
shall the one who is to die be put to death."
If the testimony is valid with two,
why did the verse spell out three?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מִתְקַיֶּימֶת הָעֵדוּת בִּשְׁנַיִם לָמָּה פָּרַט הַכָּתוּב בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of רבי יהודה בן טבאי ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the seemingly extra word 'three' in the פסוק teach?

steps.title: Three are compared to two
steps.stepSummary: The verse compares three to two: just as three witnesses can make two into זוממין, two can make three into זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse compares three to two. Just as three witnesses can make two witnesses זוממין, so too two witnesses can make three witnesses זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. 'Three' is mentioned so we can compare a group of three to a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think a pair of witnesses cannot overturn a bigger group of three. The comparison teaches that numbers do not matter here: two can disprove three through הזמה, just as three can disprove two.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare two things so they share the same law (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
Make witnesses into זוממין by proving they were elsewhere
Lying witnesses who are proven to have been somewhere else at the time

phrases.english: Rather, it is to compare three to two:
just as three can make the two into זוממין,
so too, the two can make the three into זוממין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Three' is mentioned to compare three to two, teaching that two witnesses can make three into זוממין.

steps.title: Even a hundred witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'witnesses' teaches that two can make even a hundred witnesses into זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know this works even for a hundred witnesses? The verse says 'witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה extends the rule. Two witnesses can disprove any size group, even a hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'two or three.' Repeating the word 'witnesses' is extra, so it teaches that the rule covers any number of witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
The verse teaches, saying

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, two witnesses can make any group, even a hundred, into זוממין.

phrases.english: And from where do we know even a hundred?
The verse says: "witnesses."
phrases.notes: The word 'witnesses' after 'three' is extra, since we already know the verse is talking about witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the comparison of step 39 from three to any number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses can make even a hundred witnesses into זוממין.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: all of them must be proven lying
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads the comparison differently: a group of three or more is only killed if all of them are proven זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Just as two witnesses are not killed unless both are proven זוממין, so too three are not killed unless all three are proven זוממין. And how do we know this works even for a hundred? The verse says 'witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different lesson from the same comparison of three to two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a pair is punished only if both are proven זוממין. רבי שמעון says a group of three works the same way: all of them together count as one testimony. If only some are proven זוממין, none of them are killed. The extra word 'witnesses' stretches this to a hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: Are killed (punished with death)
Both of them
All three of them

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not arguing about whether two can disprove three. He uses 'three' for a different lesson: the whole group must be proven זוממין before anyone is killed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Just as two are not killed
unless both of them are זוממין,
so too, three are not killed
unless all three of them are זוממין.
And from where do we know even a hundred?
The verse says: "witnesses."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר מָה שְׁנַיִם אֵינָן נֶהֱרָגִין עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם זוֹמְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of 'three' from the one in steps 39-40.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that a pair, a group of three, or even a hundred witnesses all count as one testimony for the rule of זוממין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group of witnesses is killed only if all of them are proven זוממין.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the third witness is not let off
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the third witness is mentioned to be strict with him, so he is punished like the other two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: The third witness was not mentioned to be lenient with him. He was mentioned to be strict with him, and to make his law like the other two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a third explanation of why the פסוק mentions 'three.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think the third witness should go free, since two witnesses were already enough and he added nothing. רבי עקיבא says no: he joined their testimony, so if they are all proven זוממין, he is punished just like them.

keyTerms.meaning: The third one
To be lenient
To be strict
Like these (the same as the others)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
The third did not come to be lenient,
but rather to be strict with him
and to make his law like these.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the first two witnesses he testified with.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לֹא בָּא הַשְּׁלִישִׁי לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of 'three,' after the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third witness, though not needed, is punished like the first two if they are all proven זוממין.

steps.title: Joining a מצוה brings full reward
steps.stepSummary: From רבי עקיבא's rule the משנה draws a קל וחומר: if joining sinners brings full punishment, joining people doing a מצוה surely brings full reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the verse punished someone who joins people doing a sin just like the sinners themselves, how much more so will God reward someone who joins people doing a מצוה just like those doing the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a lesson for life based on רבי עקיבא's rule about the third witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third witness was only an add-on, yet he is punished fully. Since God's reward is greater than His punishment, someone who only helps with a מצוה surely gets the full reward of the people doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who joins in or attaches himself to others
People doing a sin
How much more so (a קל וחומר)
Reward

steps.whatToRemember: The extra 'three' in the פסוק gets three readings: two can disprove any group (תנא קמא), all must be proven זוממין (רבי שמעון), and the extra witness is punished too (רבי עקיבא). That last one teaches that helping a מצוה earns full reward.

phrases.english: And if the verse punished
one who joins people doing a sin
like the people doing the sin,
how much more so
will He pay reward to one who joins people doing a מצוה
like those doing the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם כֵּן עָנַשׁ הַכָּתוּב לַנִּטְפָּל לְעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה כְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from רבי עקיבא's rule in step 42.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Someone who joins and helps people doing a מצוה gets the same full reward as they do.

steps.title: One disqualified witness cancels a group of three
steps.stepSummary: Using the comparison of two to three, the משנה rules that if one of three witnesses is a קרוב or פסול, the whole testimony is void, just like with two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as with two witnesses, if one of them turns out to be a relative or disqualified, their testimony is cancelled, so too with three witnesses: if one of them turns out to be a relative or disqualified, their testimony is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same comparison of 'two' and 'three' from the פסוק to teach a new rule about witnesses who are not allowed to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two witnesses, one bad witness obviously ruins the testimony, because only one valid witness is left. The comparison teaches that a group of three works the same way: the whole group is cancelled, even though two valid witnesses remain. The group is treated as one unit, so a flaw in one member spoils all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative, who may not testify for or against family
Disqualified from being a witness
Their testimony is void or cancelled
A comparison the תורה makes between two cases so they share the same laws

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two good witnesses in a group of three can still count by themselves. Once they testified together as one group, one bad witness cancels everyone's testimony.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that one קרוב or פסול inside a set of witnesses cancels the entire set.

phrases.english: And just as with two witnesses,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the פסוק the משנה quoted in step 38 (דברים 17:6), which mentions two or three witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
phrases.english: if one of them is found to be a relative or disqualified,
their testimony is void,
so too with three witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
phrases.english: if one of them is found to be a relative or disqualified,
their testimony is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה שְׁנַיִם נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another lesson drawn from the same comparison of two to three that was used for הזמה in Step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one witness in a group of three is a קרוב or פסול, the whole group's testimony is void.

steps.title: Even a hundred witnesses are cancelled by one bad witness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how we know the rule applies even to a hundred witnesses, and learns it from the word 'עדים' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this applies even to a hundred witnesses? The verse says: 'Witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a short question and answers it right away: the rule about one bad witness works for any size group, even a hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison only mentions two and three, so we might think it stops at three. The extra word 'עדים' widens the rule to any number of witnesses. This matches the pattern from Step 40, where the same word extended the rule of הזמה to a hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
The verse teaches (introduces the source from a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: From the comparison of two to three, plus the word 'עדים': a group of witnesses of any size is one unit. One bad witness cancels the whole group, just as two can make any group זוממין.

phrases.english: From where do we know that this applies even to a hundred?
The verse states: 'Witnesses.'
phrases.notes: Same extra word as in Step 40; here it stretches the 'one bad witness' rule to any number.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of Step 44 from three witnesses to any number, using the extra word as in Step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in a group of a hundred witnesses, one קרוב or פסול cancels the whole testimony, learned from the word 'עדים'.
